c.tagline: One Happy Island — Dutch-colonial color, cactus deserts, and blinding-white beaches.

taxi.fareNote: Aruba has no Uber or ride-hailing; taxis are unmetered with government-set fixed rates by zone — confirm the fare before departing. Cabs wait at hotels, the airport, and downtown, or can be booked by phone.

emergency.note: 911 is the general emergency line for ambulance and fire, and 100 reaches the police; US dollars and English are widely used, and emergency operators speak English.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Downtown Oranjestad: Caya G.F. Betico Croes Oranjestad colorful buildings

avoid.reason: Petty theft from rental cars and unattended beach bags is the main risk — never leave valuables in sight.

hood_desc: The colorful Dutch-colonial capital, where pastel gabled facades line Caya G.F. Betico Croes, the cruise terminal, and the free streetcar; the walkable base for shopping, dining, and history.
Aruba's glittering high-rise strip, packed with beachfront resorts, casinos, rooftop bars, restaurants, and the island's liveliest nightlife along a wide white-sand beach.
A calmer low-rise resort stretch along one of the Caribbean's widest, most photographed beaches, framed by the iconic fofoti trees; ideal for a relaxed, romantic stay.
The inland district behind Palm Beach, a hub of restaurants, supermarkets, and easy access to the Alto Vista Chapel and California Lighthouse; a convenient, local-feeling base near the action.

The upscale northwestern tip of calm, clear coves — Malmok, Arashi, and Boca Catalina — prized for snorkeling, the Antilla shipwreck, and quiet villas away from the resort crowds; best for a serene, water-focused stay.

water.note: Desalinated tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Arubus runs roughly 6:00 AM to about 9:00-11:00 PM (later on the Palm Beach-Oranjestad corridor), with reduced Sunday and holiday service; the free downtown streetcar runs daytime hours only.
transit.note: Public transit centers on Arubus, the island bus network linking Oranjestad with Palm Beach, Eagle Beach, and San Nicolas, plus a free vintage streetcar (tram) looping through downtown Oranjestad; most visitors also use taxis or rental cars.
transit.pay: Pay the Arubus driver in cash (about Afl. 2.60 / US$2.60 one-way, or buy a smart card at the Oranjestad terminal); US dollars are accepted. The downtown streetcar is free.

car.idp: Not required (US, Canadian, and most licenses valid up to 3 months)

ferry: Renaissance Marina water taxi to Renaissance Private Island

transit.m: Arubus Airport route to Oranjestad (~20 min)
Taxi to Oranjestad (10 min, fixed fare)
Taxi to Palm Beach (20 min, fixed fare)

tip.r: A 15% service charge is often added to hotel and restaurant bills; if it isn't, 15-20% is standard, and tipping taxis and housekeeping is appreciated.
